title: 35 Stocks Went In. These 3 Came Out on Top.
description: And there was a pretty clear #1
body_html:
Happy Thursday! Hope your investments are going as planned. We had a huge list to work through this week, 35 companies, narrowed all the way down to just 3.

Midweek Movers continues to grow in popularity, and this week gave us a particularly strong final group. Several of the names that survived the cut are in the mining sector and have already started moving, which lines up well with what we’ve been discussing around precious metals and miners over the past few days.

One important note before we get into the rankings: just because a stock was a prior winner, or a pick of my own, doesn’t mean it wins again today. Frontline, for example, was a stock we began tracking in February and ultimately became a winner in the March Midweek Movers. The trend is still intact, but at this stage I’m more interested in finding the names that haven’t already made their move.

A blast from the past, TTM Technologies, TTMI 10.31%↑, was another one. Ultimately this stock ran over 557%. It treated me well in 2025, and admittedly, one of the members here made a much larger % than I did. No, I did not catch all of that move…the point is to catch a piece of trend. Not time tops or bottoms.

But a stock appearing on the StockTok Screener last year doesn’t automatically make it a winner this year. In fact, TTMI ranked toward the bottom of the list this time around.

Subscribe now

Getting attached to prior price action is called “anchoring bias,” and it can be costly. Anchoring bias is where there is emotional attachment, or hindsight analysis, of a stock that previously ran upwards well, but has since descended. People with anchoring bias often think they are getting discounts (and sometimes they are, but not often), and begin fighting trends trying to relive prior price action.

Regardless, that was a fantastic ride while it lasted!

I do pride myself a little on being able to find decent stocks, and I’m really happy with how the StockTok screener has performed. After several years of this, I think we’ve proven there’s a method to the madness. 🤪

Ok. Gloating done.

Now, here’s the full list of tickers:

Before continuing, please remember to like ❤️ and re-stack 🔄

Bottom Tier: , , and IVPAF

The very first thing I do is check to see if the price action is below the 200 day moving average. You can’t hit a local high, 52 week high or all time high, if price action is trending below there. Period. Though any one of these may reverse at anytime, trend is not on our side. Do not fight trends! You do not need to get “best price” or go dumpster diving. In fact, if it “feels” expensive…its likely to get more expensive…ie, more profitable for you.

Share

Weakest Relative Strength:

We have 35 tickers. I want to have the stocks that have the strongest bullish trends, relative to the S&P 500. Here I was able to quickly eliminate 14 stocks. This does not mean that they are “bearish” per say. But they just do not have as much momentum as I would like to see. All of these stocks had relative strength (RS), below 70.

Understandably, Google and Mastercard may come as surprises, but these are simply so large of a market cap, that achieving super performance, is unlikely.

Special shout out to Deutsche Bank, . Though it ranks towards the bottom, I liked price action moving up and breaking highs. I speculate it will do well, It just did not have enough strength to top the stocks in this list.

Bad Entry Criteria:

You may have a great company, but if your entry sucks, so will your portfolio. Some of these stocks, like AYA, AVAH and Twist Bioscience, have ran so much from the consolidation breakout, that I have no idea if they are likely to continue, or ready for an imminent reversal. I like to get into a winning position, then begin the guessing game of where a top is at. Target has been running since December… after crashing -68%. But has not put in a higher high on the macro trends, and very little confirmation bounces locally.

Mixed or Bad Earnings:

I know many of you care about fundamentals. So I prefer to bring you great stocks with strong chart structure, great entries, and good fundamentals. Each of these stocks, either had declining earnings annually and/or declining cashflow annually.

Now, the remaining stocks meet all of our basic requirements for purchasing. They meet our trend requirements (with strength), have earnings trending upward, and three also meet our SEPA, specific entry point analysis, criteria.
